name: Taichung International Airport / Ching Chuang Kang Air Base
before:
Taichung's airport, sixth busiest in Taiwan, with scheduled flights to China, Hong Kong, Japan, Macau, South Korea and Vietnam.

It is a useful alternative to flying into Taipei for a client based in central Taiwan, though the network is regional rather than long haul, so most itineraries will still route through Taoyuan.

It is often still listed as Ching Chuan Kang Airport, so both names turn up in supplier systems.

Civilian services began on 5 March 2004, replacing the old Shuinan Airport nearer the city centre. It was promoted to international status on 3 January 2017 and renamed Taichung International Airport at that point.
after:
Taichung's airport, with scheduled flights to mainland China, Hong Kong, Japan, Macau, South Korea and Vietnam.

It is a useful alternative to flying into Taipei for a client based in central Taiwan, though the network is regional rather than long haul, so most itineraries will still route through Taoyuan.

Ching Chuan Kang Airport is its other name, so both turn up in supplier systems.

Civilian flights moved here from the old Shuinan Airport in March 2004.
